title: RE Services Personal Trading in Non-Perpetual Securities Policy

tiers.name: RE Services staff
tiers.description: All staff within the RE Services business unit of the Perpetual Entities (Perpetual Trust Services Limited, The Trust Company (RE Services) Limited, The Trust Company (Sydney Airports) Limited), who administer schemes such as MXT ('non-Perpetual securities'). Treated as 'Employees' under the (unattached) Group Policy but expressly excluded from that Group Policy's 'Restricted Employees' category.

tiers.name: Senior Manager, Risk Manager, or Corporate Client Manager, RE Services legal counsel
tiers.description: Named roles whose trading in non-Perpetual securities must be approved in writing by the Business Unit Head.

tiers.name: Business Unit Head
tiers.description: The RE Services Business Unit Head; their own trading must be approved in writing by the General Manager, Managed Fund Services. Also the only person who may approve amendments to this Policy.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: A further non-trading period runs (c) from identification/reporting of a potential disclosing event to a Perpetual Entity (as defined in the RE Services Continuous and Material/Significant Events Policy) until resolution and/or disclosure to members, and (d) from awareness of a scheme amendment until it is implemented and/or reported to members; no specific officer is named as empowered to declare these, and confidentiality of the trigger is not addressed.

rules.detail: Not mentioned in this Policy. It applies to 'personal trading in non-Perpetual securities' without defining whether that includes derivatives, and defers substantive Insider Trading, third-party procurement, conflicts and high-volume trading rules to an unattached Group Policy.
Redemptions of non-Perpetual securities (which would include MXT units) must be held for at least three months.

bespoke_clauses.topic: substantive terms sit in an unattached Group Policy
bespoke_clauses.clause: RE Services staff are included in the definition of Employees for the purposes of the Group Policy – Personal Trading in non-Perpetual Securities ... (a) Prohibition of Insider Trading (b) Prohibition on procuring or encouraging third parties to trade (c) Conflicts of interest (d) High volume personal trading. Under the Group Policy, RE Services staff are not included in the definition of Restricted Employees.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This document does not itself contain any derivatives, hedging, margin lending or secured financing rules; those (if any) would be in the referenced Group Policy or the separate Group Policy – Personal Trading in Perpetual Securities, neither of which is in evidence, so a collar verdict cannot be given with confidence from this document alone.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval granted pursuant to this Policy is valid for that business day only. Where the RE Services staff member has failed to act on that approval, a new approval must be sought to trade on another business day.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any dealing approved under this Policy (e.g. entering a put/call leg) must execute the same business day it is approved, which is a tight window for coordinating a bank-structured collar and loan drawdown.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Redemptions: Position must be held for at least three months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As MXT is a unit trust, exit is via redemption rather than on-market sale; this minimum hold constrains the earliest point at which a collared position could be unwound by redemption.

summary: This document alone does not permit a definitive funded-collar verdict. It is a narrow internal conduct policy for RE Services staff administering schemes like MXT, requiring written same-day pre-approval of trading (from the Business Unit Head, or from the General Manager, Managed Fund Services for the Business Unit Head), a maintained personal trading register, avoidance of two calendar non-trading periods tied to financial statement releases, event-driven non-trading periods while a disclosing event or scheme amendment is unresolved, and a three-month minimum hold before redemption. It expressly defers the substantive Insider Trading, third-party procurement, conflicts-of-interest and high-volume-trading rules to a 'Group Policy – Personal Trading in Non-Perpetual Securities' that is referenced but not included here, and separately points to a 'Group Policy – Personal Trading in Perpetual Securities' for trading in Perpetual's own securities. No provision addresses derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance, short selling, stock lending or CFDs, so whether a purchased put, written call or a loan secured on the units would be permitted cannot be determined without obtaining those Group Policies. Subject to that gap, nothing visible here would block a collar outside the stated closed periods and the three-month hold, provided same-day approval is obtained for each dealing.
